record.paper_title: Padua points and “fake” nodes for polynomial approximation: old, new and open problems
record.original_question: Let Ω be a compact subset of R^d. For degree-m polynomials P bounded by 1 on Ω, define the Dubiner metric by μΩ(x,y)=sup (1/m)|arccos(P(x))-arccos(P(y))| over such P. Are nearly optimal interpolation point sets on Ω asymptotically equidistributed with respect to this Dubiner metric?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. Nearly optimal interpolation points on a compact Ω ⊂ R^d are asymptotically equidistributed with respect to the Dubiner metric on Ω.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact set. For a positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal{P}_m$ denote the space of real polynomials of degree at most $m$ in $d$ variables. Define the Dubiner (pseudo)metric on $\Omega$ by
$$\mu_\Omega(x,y) \;=\; \sup\Big\{\tfrac{1}{m}\big|\arccos P(x) - \arccos P(y)\big| \;:\; m\ge 1,\; P\in\mathcal{P}_m,\; \|P\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le 1\Big\},$$
for $x,y\in\Omega$. For each $m$, let $N_m = \dim \mathcal{P}_m|_\Omega$ and let $X_m=\{x_1^{(m)},\dots,x_{N_m}^{(m)}\}\subset\Omega$ be a sequence of unisolvent interpolation arrays whose Lebesgue constants grow at most polynomially in $m$ ("nearly optimal" interpolation points). Consider the associated normalized counting (empirical) measures
$$\nu_m \;=\; \frac{1}{N_m}\sum_{j=1}^{N_m}\delta_{x_j^{(m)}}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every compact $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and every such nearly optimal sequence $(X_m)$, the measures $\nu_m$ converge weakly, as $m\to\infty$, to a measure that is equidistributed with respect to the Dubiner metric $\mu_\Omega$ on $\Omega$ (i.e., the points $X_m$ are asymptotically uniformly distributed in the Dubiner metric).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, originally due to Dubiner, that nearly optimal polynomial interpolation point sets on a compact set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ are asymptotically equidistributed with respect to the Dubiner metric, remains open in general. Verifications are known only in special cases (e.g., the interval, the square via Padua-like points, spherical triangles), and the Dubiner metric itself is explicitly known only on a few domains. No general proof or disproof appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: From Dubiner metric to Padua points (De Marchi, slides)
status_evidence.snippet: Nearly-optimal interpolation points on a compact are asymptotically equidistributed w.r.t. the Dubiner metric; explicit Dubiner metric is known in very few cases.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open problem with only special-case verifications.

status_evidence.title: Near-Optimal Polynomial Interpolation on Spherical Triangles
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs near-optimal interpolation points and discusses asymptotic distribution with respect to Dubiner-type metrics on specific domains.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works treat only particular geometries, consistent with the general conjecture remaining unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Sets of near-optimal points for interpolation on the square
status_evidence.snippet: Families of points on the square are asymptotically equidistributed in the Dubiner metric.
status_evidence.claim: Equidistribution is established in the square case but not in general.
